sentences.text: The Automatic Identification System, or AIS, broadcasts a vessel’s identity, position, course and speed over VHF data channels.
With an AIS receiver you can see a ship’s name and call her directly, and your plotter can calculate the closest point of approach.
Class A transponders are required on many commercial vessels, and Class B units are designed for smaller boats.
Many vessels carry no AIS at all, so it never replaces a proper lookout.
And seeing a vessel on AIS doesn’t mean you’re in sight of her under the Navigation Rules.
